text:
Maria (infra): Heads-up: after yesterday's CU12 image rebase we started seeing a weird modprobe/RTLD failure on a subset of nodes in eu-west. Provisioner marks them green but containers fail to start (kubelet crashloop / initrd errors).

Sasha (oncall): seeing the same on canaries in eu-west-2. Nodes are 'provisioning' in the dashboard but GPU drivers appear loaded. Quick log snippets: `modprobe: ERROR: could not insert 'nvidia_uvm': No such device` and `ld.so: /opt/redwood/lib/libstdc++.so.6: version GLIBCXX_3.4.29' not found`.

Kevin: that screams compiler/runtime mismatch — images built with `gcc-13` toolchain paired with toolkit12 libs, host kernel and distro libstdc++ older. Options: (1) vendor `libstdc++` into the image (ugly), (2) rebuild images with older toolchain, or (3) install compat libs on host via provisioner.

Dave: important: this is spilling into provisioning backoff loops — provisioner retries, nodes bounce, API starts failing to allocate new GPU pods. We're seeing capacity reported down in eu-west by ~15%. That is hitting Dedicated customer queues and inflating fallback usage. Cost team FYI: fallback to burst-hosted is running hotter.

Harini: APAC reported increased latency because eu-west fallback pushed traffic to ap-southeast for some customers with affinity rules. Need quick mitigation to avoid cost/regional SLA hits.

Kevin: repro steps I used locally: pull `redwood/cu12:2026-03-rebase`, run `ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so` and `strings libstdc++.so.6 | grep GLIBCXX_3.4.29` -> missing. Also `nm -D /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so | grep __cudaRegisterFatBinary` showed symbols present but dynamic loader can't link to newer libstdc++.

Sasha (oncall): NCCL noise too on affected nodes: `NCCL WARN All gpus failed to open nvml` followed by `unhandled system error` when container tries to init NVML. Might be kernel module probe ordering + toolchain mismatch causing dlopen fails.

Maria (infra): Root cause hypothesis: the new CU12 images were built with system gcc13, shipping newer libstdc++ which clashes when the container picks host libs (we use ldconfig shims during provisioning). On some host kernels the `ld-linux` path picks host libstdc++ and fails to satisfy GLIBCXX symbols -> resulting in early dlopen failures for NV driver pieces.

Dave: So two failure modes: (A) `modprobe` fails because kernel module load order gets hung when dlopen of helper libs fails, and (B) containerized runtime ends up using partial host libs leading to segfaults. Both cause provisioning loops.

Harini: Immediate mitigation suggestion: pin the CU12 rollout: flip `infra.provisioner.toolkit.rollout=off` for eu-west and ap-southeast in flags-service, revert to CU11 images for those regions. We should also mark affected hosts `drain: true` for GPU scheduling to prevent user-facing failures.

Kevin: I can prepare a one-line image patch that bundles `libstdc++.so.6.0.30` into `/opt/redwood/compat/` and updates `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` at process start as a hotfix. Less risky than a full rollback. But the provisioning shim might still prefer host libs.

Maria (infra): prefer hard rollback to CU11 for safety — less unknowns and cheaper in ops time. Kevin, please prepare the compat patch as a stopgap if we need a faster patch while rollback starts.

Sasha (oncall): I'm kicking a rollback runbook: `runbook/provisioner/cu12-rollback` -> step 1: disable the rollout flag, step 2: push cu11 images to canaries, step 3: monitor `provisioner.queue` and `gpu-pool-util`. I'm on it now. tagging @deploy-bot to start the canary rollback.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback requested by Sasha. Initiating image switch in eu-west canaries. ETA 12m.

ops-bot: Alert created: INFRA-PRV-3742 "CU12 image rebase caused libstdc++/modprobe failures" assigned to infra oncall. Priority: P1.

Dave: Postmortem todo: analyze why the provisioner didn't detect ABI mismatch during our preflight (we run `ldd` checks but they were false-negative). Add a step to validate `GLIBCXX` symbol set and NVML probe order on hosts. Also compute cost delta: fallback-hosting + increased burst capacity across regions.

Harini: Noted. I'll open a billing impact ticket and notify Account Execs for affected Dedicated customers. Also will temp increase quota in other regions to keep SLAs for high-tier customers.

Kevin: I'll assemble a small repro and a PR for the compat image. Maria, coordinate with release to block further CU12 pushes until we have the kernel/module ordering fix and a packaging guideline for libstdc++.

Maria (infra): thanks — I'll update the incident channel and the rollback progress here. If rollback clears provisioning and GPUs return, we'll reopen a lower priority task for a safer CU12 re-introduction with the shim included.

Sasha (oncall): rollback completed on canaries, monitoring cluster. Early signs: `provisioner.queue` length down, GPU pod starts succeed. Keeping this thread pinned until we confirm full eu-west roll. :thumbsup:

Dave: Good catch team — let's keep the postmortem short and actionable.
